findings.issue: The schema comment quotes the carriers' own kit line ("Normal attacks deal true damage. This effect is continuous") and names both carriers. prepare-cross-family-packet.ts builds the blind roles' types-redacted.ts by dropping only lines that name the target slug/name/tokens, so for a future blind run on either bunny the slug-naming line 752 is stripped but the quoted kit prose on 749-751 survives and tells the blind role exactly which field encodes that line — the same leak shape the cinderella-crystal-wave review flagged for the `pierceModes` "(CCW: SR only)" comment.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the types.ts comment generic ("true-flavored normals only while in one of these kit modes; resolves once at setup like pierceModes; also flavors swap shots") and leave carrier names + the kit quote to the override notes / DECISIONS, which already carry them.

findings.issue: The new undeclared-mode check exists for trueNormalsModes only; its stated twin `pierceModes` has no equivalent check (grep: validate-structural.ts never mentions pierceModes), so the two siblings are no longer wired identically. Not a defect in this diff — the extra guard is correct — but the asymmetry is the kind of drift the next author will copy.

unexercisedScope: (1) The only engine consumer of the resolved flag is `trueFlavor` on the two firePull dealDamage calls (sim.ts:4525, 4558); the second is the PIERCE_CORE_DOUBLE body hit, which neither carrier reaches (no hasPierce/pierceModes on either bunny) — behaviour there is by inspection identical to the existing hasTrueNormals path, not by test. (2) Inertness for non-setters rests on `skills.trueNormalsModes` being undefined → `?? false`; the full regression suite passing unchanged is the evidence, plus resolveSkills only copies the field from the override. (3) The web client runs the same engine via `prepared[idx].mode`; `rg hasPierce|pierceModes|hasTrueNormals|trueNormalsModes web/src` returns nothing, so no web registry enumerates these top-level keys and nothing there needs a sibling entry. (4) `scripts/blind-rebuild/code-bundle/*` is a hand-copied engine snapshot with no generator in the tree (rg for `code-bundle` finds only SKILL.md and a manual-review doc) — it is stale by design and not a registry for this field. (5) `scripts/kit-autonomy/blind/types-redacted.ts` is regenerated per gauntlet run from types.ts, so the committed copy is not a missed registry (see NOTE 1 for the comment-leak angle). (6) Docs: STATE.md:327, engine-modeling-gaps.md:133, damage-calculation.md:223 and damage-bucket-matrix.md already carry the field in the uncommitted doc edits; game-mechanics.md never names hasTrueNormals so has no sibling line to update.
